name: Ali Haydar
headline: Application developer with a completed apprenticeship as Informatiker EFZ Applikationsentwicklung, continuing his studies at WISS Schule Zürich toward Dipl. Informatiker HF / Professional Bachelor.
summary: IT professional in development with a background in application development and a strong interest in building useful software.
Wants to turn the IT knowledge he has gained over the years into increasingly capable, practical work.
Is building on the knowledge from his IT education and practical experience.

Currently studying at WISS Schule Zürich toward Dipl. Informatiker HF / Professional Bachelor.

experience.role: Apprentice in application development (no other job title)

A client project in parcel management: the web application for Grenzlager GmbH (see projects).
experience.howHeWorked: Focused on delivering the best possible result for each client. Worked closely with his team, followed their guidance and instructions, and received very positive feedback on his work.

work: Responsible for how the dealership and its vehicles are presented to customers.
First point of contact for customers, looking after them personally.

ipa: IPA means "Individuelle Praktische Arbeit", the final practical project of the Swiss vocational training. For his successfully completed IPA, he extended existing software to automate the handling of uncollected parcels. Details are in the project "IPA Final Project" below.

projects.name: Grenzlager GmbH: Warehouse Management Web Application
projects.context: A client project of BETA Solutions GmbH, developed during his apprenticeship there.
projects.description: Developed a web application for Grenzlager GmbH, a package reception service near the Swiss border. The system is in use by the company to manage customer parcels, notifications, and collections.
projects.extensions: Extended it with automated reminders and storage fee management through email and WhatsApp. This extension was his IPA final project; the web application itself was not part of the IPA.

projects.name: IPA Final Project: Grenzlager GmbH Automated Parcel Reminders and Fee Management
projects.description: Designed and implemented an extension to Grenzlager GmbH's warehouse management system that sends collection reminders by email and WhatsApp, calculates storage fees, and tracks overdue parcels and notifications.
projects.result: Assessed by cantonal examination experts as part of the Swiss vocational qualification process; passed.

projects.name: AI Guide: Personal AI Chat for Recruiters
projects.technology: Node.js, WebSockets, JavaScript, a language model (locally with Ollama, online through the Groq API)
projects.description: The AI guide on his portfolio website that answers visitors' questions about his professional background. Answers stream live over WebSockets from a language model.
projects.features: Uses only facts Ali has approved, blocks prompt injection and off-topic requests before they reach the model, checks every answer sentence by sentence before visitors see it, and answers in English and German.

projects.name: Person Manager
projects.description: Java application for managing and displaying personal data, with a graphical user interface (GUI) for viewing and editing entries, navigating between entries, and editing functions.

projects.description: A classic chess game implemented in Java.

projects.name: Flappy Bird
projects.description: A Flappy Bird game in React where the player taps the screen to navigate a bird through pipes.

languagesOnProjectsPage: On his projects page, Ali names C++, Java, JavaScript, and SQL among the programming languages he has worked with.
goals: Looking for a role where he can contribute to software development, keep programming, learn from experienced colleagues, and bring what he studies into real projects.
aboutThisBot: Ali built this AI bot so employers and other visitors can learn about his experience, interests, and goals by asking questions directly. It runs on a Node.js server with WebSockets and a language model (locally with Ollama, online through the Groq API), with rules against made-up facts and prompt injection.
